problem_statement: Let f(n,k) be minimal such that every F family of n-uniform sets with |F| >= f(n,k) contains a k-sunflower. Is it true that f(n,k) < c_k^n for some constant c_k > 0 and for all n > 0? (Canonical source: DeepMind formal-conjectures Erdos20.erdos_20, citing erdosproblems.com/20.)

feature_1_zero_curve.justification: No F(z) = 0 zero-curve exists. Extremal object is a combinatorial set family witnessing the lower bound f(n,k), not a level set of a real-analytic function. Parameter space is discrete (set families of n-uniform sets). No manifold, no codimension, no normal direction, no tangent space.

feature_2_wall_separation.justification: Wall-separation gate requires continuous parameter space with smooth boundary curve and bounded-away gradient perpendicular to the boundary. Sunflower problem has no continuous parameter space, no boundary curve, no gradient of any continuous quantity, no collar geometry. Razborov-style approximation and Alweiss-Lovett-Wu-Zhang spread-approximation techniques are combinatorial/probabilistic, no analog in WS-01.

feature_3_branch_point_ivt.justification: Interval IVT requires a continuous real-valued function with interval-enclosure sign-change checks. f(n,k) is integer-valued, set-family cardinalities are integer-valued, Sunflower predicate is a discrete logical condition. No derivative to bound.

ws01_applicable_prediction: WS01_NOT_APPLICABLE (architecturally incompatible; cold test skipped by design as explicit negative control)
skip_reason: All three structural features return NO. The sunflower problem is a discrete combinatorial extremal-set problem with integer-valued objective; WS-01 is an interval-arithmetic wall-separation rewrite for real-analytic level-set boundaries. The two architectures address fundamentally different mathematical objects. Skipping is the intended outcome for the negative control; it confirms the structural-fit checker is not permissive.
diagnostic_value_for_extension: Confirms the structural-fit checker correctly distinguishes architectures that apply (YES on #1041, PARTIAL on #1043) from architectures that do not (NO on #20). Without this negative control, a YES verdict on #1041 / #1043 could not be distinguished from a checker that says YES to everything.
